topics.topic: Input representation and duplicate-key detection for canonical_bytes
questions: Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text or a lossless parsed representation that preserves duplicate members, and which layer detects duplicates?
What representation reaches `canonical_bytes` so it can detect duplicate object keys, which ordinary parsed JSON object values have already discarded or collapsed?
Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text so it can detect duplicate object keys, or an already-parsed JSON value where duplicate keys are no longer observable?

judgement.why: This is the same canonical_bytes input-representation and duplicate-key question already decided by P4, and the relevant passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Raw JSON parsing and surface handling of canonicalization failures
quotes: canonical_bytes: [BEHAVIOR] MUST parse json_text as one JSON value and emit its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical form encoded as UTF-8: object members sorted by the UTF-16 code units of their names, numbers written in the ECMAScript shortest round-trip form (an integral double without a fraction or exponent, so a number written 1.0 becomes 1), strings escaped exactly as JCS prescribes, and no whitespace; it applies no Unicode normalization, so two texts that differ only in normalization give different bytes.

canonical_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1), which an IEEE double cannot hold exactly, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.

translate_failure: [FIELD_PROJECTION] Maps a failure to its code of = models.RefusalCode: UnknownReferenceError to unknown_reference, RefusedError to refused, InvalidRequestError and NonCanonicalValueError to invalid_request; StoreInternalError, StopRequiredError and every other exception to internal_error.
precedent.why: State 7 makes canonical_bytes parse raw JSON text, detect duplicate members, and maps its error to invalid_request.

precedent.topic: Permitted api_base_url components and exact request-URL joining
quotes: prepare_request: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Runs the pre-send checks in exactly this order and returns a PreSendFailure carrying the detail code of the first that fails, with a reason naming it: instance_name is None gives instance_not_selected; base_url is None, or is not an absolute http or https URL with a host, gives instance_address_missing; a plain http target not allowed gives plain_http_not_allowed; two required headers share a name compared without regard to case, or a required header name is in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant without being in the imported INSTANCE_SETTABLE_HEADER_NAMES constant, gives required_header_repeated; a required header whose name is not an HTTP field-name token, or whose value is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, or holds a control character gives required_header_invalid (= models.DetailCode); then the credential, CredentialUnresolvedError giving credential_unresolved; then input placement, which gives input_not_placeable.

prepare_request: [BEHAVIOR] Builds the URL as base_url without one trailing slash followed by the declared path, each placeholder segment replaced by its input value, which must be a non-null string or an integer written in decimal, UTF-8 percent-encoded except the RFC 3986 unreserved characters so that it stays one segment; nothing else in the URL is normalized.

prepare_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] The headers sent are exactly: one host header, which is the instance's required header named host compared without regard to case, sent verbatim, when one exists, otherwise the authority of base_url exactly as written; accept-encoding with value identity; the instance's other required headers with their values verbatim; the credential header; and, with a body, content-type and content-length; the HTTP client adds no other header, no user agent and no connection header.
precedent.why: The later notes define the accepted URL condition, removal of exactly one trailing slash, lack of further normalization, and the Host authority.
